title: What the Motors and the Battery Allow: Top Speed, Acceleration and Climb From a Drive Train, and Which of the Motors or the Grip Is the One That Runs Out First

questions.question: What gives a brushed motor its force at the wheel?
options: The torque-speed line, through the gearbox, over the wheel radius
The battery's capacity in watt hours
questions.explanation: The motor gives its stall torque at rest and none at its no load speed, on a straight line between. The gearbox multiplies it and the wheel's radius turns it into force.

questions.question: A battery of 0.5 ohm cut the standing acceleration from 4.54 to:
questions.explanation: A standing start draws the most current, and 0.5 ohm of internal resistance dropped the bus below three quarters of its voltage.

questions.question: The top speed on level gravel was:
options: 1.67 m/s, under the no load speed
questions.explanation: The motors' force falls to zero at 1.83 m/s, and rolling resistance and drag stop the vehicle a little short of that. On a 10 degree slope it was 0.99 m/s.

questions.question: On gravel the limit on the acceleration was the:
questions.explanation: Gravel holds a slope of 22.3 degrees and the motors can start on 25.6, so the tyres give out first. On tarmac, which holds 38.1, it was the motors.

questions.question: Why is it money wasted to buy stronger motors for a grip limited robot?
options: Stronger motors drain the battery faster
The tyres cannot hold the extra force, so the acceleration does not change
It is not wasted: more force is always more acceleration
questions.explanation: The force that reaches the ground is capped by the grip. Past that cap the wheels spin, whatever the motor could give.

questions.question: Why was the vehicle tuned on a fresh battery wrong on a tired one?
options: A tired battery sags more under the standing current
Its voltage is higher at rest
The motors draw less from it
questions.explanation: As a battery ages its internal resistance rises, so the same standing current pulls the bus down further and the acceleration with it.
